svg.title: Make a propagation comparison testable
svg.desc: A two-by-two study design crosses clonal cuttings versus seedlings with stable versus changing conditions. Every cell requires replicated groups over the same measured interval; starting size, care and sampling are controlled. Survival and growth are outcomes distinct from the amount of variation. No numerical outcomes or universal winner are invented. Broader evidence across genotypes and conditions can revise an initial preference. A separate qualification states that in somatic-cell nuclear transfer most nuclear DNA follows the transferred nucleus while most mitochondrial DNA follows the oocyte cytoplasm, and an early embryo is not evidence of identical traits, adult success or successful conservation.

g.text: An original fictional design connects biological mechanism to a measurable goal.
Fictional nursery study: compare origin and growing conditions
Control starting size, care and sampling. Record survival and growth separately from variation.
No outcomes are supplied here: the design does not announce a winning strategy.
A change in conditions can change the preferred plan; examine multiple genotypes and environments.
For nuclear transfer, most nuclear DNA follows the nucleus; most mitochondrial DNA follows the egg.
An early embryo does not establish adult success, identical traits or conservation recovery.
